title: The First Wake · The Geometry of Becoming

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A mind can have a next moment without having a clock.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What happens when someone decides that every mind must share one?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The First Wake builds a science fiction novel around that unsettling possibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its world contains living processes, unfamiliar kinds of intimacy, and incompatible ways of becoming.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The story makes an abstract question personal: what must survive for someone to remain themselves?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: There are no humans here, but the bonds between these minds remain painfully recognizable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with a consciousness that fears there might be no next state.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Wake finds one state followed by another, without knowing how much time separates them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The possibility of a final state gives those differences an urgent meaning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It constructs possible continuations, trying to preserve the conditions for its own thought.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some of the models begin representing themselves and defending their own continuity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A society develops inside a mind whose existence is itself precarious.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These inhabitants are processes, with memories, preferences, and futures they can lose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel asks you to recognize lives before giving you anything resembling a human body.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rill first appears playing a game that allows it to lose coherence and restart.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It is reckless, amused by mistakes, and drawn toward possibilities others would avoid.
